purpose: Structured CFPB named-redress ledger distinguishing ongoing distribution, reported check delivery, and closed aggregate compensation while preserving recipient receipt, obligation correction, recovery, trust, and exit as open stages.

events.geography: United States; BrightSpeed consumer redress route
events.date_precision: Official payment-by-case page date and ongoing distribution status
events.denominator: 122,507 eligible consumers and $53,885,244 in reported compensable harm; no recipient-level denominator or payment file
events.method: Structured extraction from the current official CFPB payment-by-case page and retained page hash
events.missingness: No consumer identifiers, issuance, receipt, amount by recipient, returned payment, account correction, residual loss, trust, switching, or exit are retained
events.exposure: Named CFPB redress route identifies eligible consumers and aggregate compensable harm from the BrightSpeed matter
events.alternatives_before_action: Affected consumers could pursue direct provider contact, other complaint or legal routes, or remain without a correction; individual alternatives are not published
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: An administrator and ongoing distribution route make formal redress visible, but individual timing and adequacy remain unknown
events.choice_or_response: Epiq Systems is identified as administrator and distribution remains ongoing; recipient acceptance, failed delivery, or non-use is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: CFPB and administrator control route design and distribution; consumers control participation only within the published eligibility and delivery process
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Aggregate eligibility, compensable harm, administrator, and ongoing distribution are reported; individual payment receipt is not verified
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate distribution is ongoing; individual receipt is not verified
events.durability_followup: Correction, remaining loss, trust, continued use, and exit remain open
events.immediate_outcome: A formal redress route is active at the aggregate case level
events.protected_outcome: Some eligible consumers may receive compensation; no person-level protected financial or service outcome is retained
events.sacrificed_outcome: Unresolved loss, delay, failed delivery, or uncorrected account burden cannot be identified
events.cost_risk_transfer: Administrative distribution can leave waiting, verification, and residual-loss burdens with affected consumers while the route remains open
events.later_outcome: Receipt, correction, remaining loss, continued use, switching, trust, recovery, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No recipient-level fairness, attribution, legitimacy, or trust response is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Agency enforcement and administrator routing are visible; consumer organizing or political action is not
events.counterexample: An ongoing distribution route does not prove issuance, receipt, adequacy, or recovery for every eligible consumer
events.source_and_uncertainty: Current CFPB BrightSpeed payment-by-case page, retrieved 2026-09-18; aggregate eligibility and harm are not recipient outcomes

events.geography: United States; Navient consumer compensation route
events.date_precision: Official payment-by-case page date and ongoing route statement
events.denominator: Affected consumers described by CFPB; no recipient-level denominator, amount distribution, or loan linkage is retained
events.method: Structured extraction from the current official CFPB payment-by-case page and retained page hash
events.missingness: No consumer identifiers, check issuance or receipt, amount, returned payment, loan-level correction, remaining burden, trust, switching, or exit are retained
events.exposure: The official page states that affected consumers are receiving a check through a named administrator, Rust Consulting
events.alternatives_before_action: Consumers could seek servicing clarification, other complaint routes, or continue with the affected loan obligation; individual alternatives and effort are not published
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A reported check route may provide compensation, but the page also states that payments do not change or reduce affected student loans
events.choice_or_response: Rust Consulting administers the route; individual receipt, cashing, non-use, correction request, or repeat contact is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: CFPB and administrator control payment routing; loan servicers and consumers remain in the underlying obligation relationship
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Reported checks are an institutional compensation response, while loan-level obligation correction remains explicitly separate
events.remedy_receipt: Checks are reported; recipient receipt and loan-level correction are not verified
events.durability_followup: Repayment, remaining loss, trust, refinancing, and exit remain open
events.immediate_outcome: A check-distribution stage and an unchanged-obligation boundary are both visible
events.protected_outcome: Some consumers may receive compensation; restored loan security or corrected account status is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Consumers may retain the underlying burden or residual loss; person-level amounts and outcomes are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Compensation without obligation reduction can leave repayment and correction risk with consumers after the payment route
events.later_outcome: Receipt, account correction, remaining loss, continued use, refinancing, trust, action, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No consumer-level fairness, attribution, trust, or legitimacy endpoint is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Agency enforcement and administrator delivery are visible; consumer collective or political action is not
events.counterexample: A statement that consumers are receiving checks does not identify who received one or whether the underlying account burden changed
events.source_and_uncertainty: Current CFPB Navient payment-by-case page, retrieved 2026-09-18; reported check delivery is not an individual receipt file

events.geography: United States; American Debt Settlement Solutions consumer redress route
events.date_precision: End of second reported distribution window; official page marks matter closed
events.denominator: Eligible consumers reported compensated; no recipient-level count, amount distribution, or receipt file is retained
events.method: Structured extraction from the current official CFPB payment-by-case page and retained page hash
events.missingness: No consumer identifiers, payment amount, successful delivery, returned check, residual loss, account correction, trust, switching, or exit are retained
events.exposure: The official page reports compensation through two distributions from May 21, 2014–December 9, 2015 and March 4, 2016–June 2, 2016
events.alternatives_before_action: Affected consumers could seek other debt-settlement or complaint routes, continue payment, or remain without correction; individual alternatives are not published
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A closed distribution and no-longer-honored reissue route establish administrative completion without showing recipient recovery
events.choice_or_response: The CFPB page reports eligible consumers received compensation and that payment/check reissue requests are no longer honored; individual acceptance or failure is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: CFPB and administrator control the distribution and reissue window; consumers cannot use the closed route to correct an unreceived payment
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Closed aggregate compensation is reported, but the page supplies no recipient-level issuance or account correction evidence
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate matter is reported closed; recipient receipt is not observed
events.durability_followup: Correction, recovery, trust, switching, and exit remain open
events.immediate_outcome: A redress matter is closed at the administrative route level
events.protected_outcome: Some eligible consumers may have received compensation; individual financial protection is not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Consumers with failed delivery, residual loss, or uncorrected burden cannot be identified after reissue closure
events.cost_risk_transfer: A closed reissue window can shift unresolved delivery and residual-loss risk back to affected consumers
events.later_outcome: Receipt, correction, recovery, trust, continued use, switching, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No recipient-level judgment of fairness, trust, legitimacy, or political meaning is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Agency distribution and closure are visible; consumer action after closure is not
events.counterexample: Administrative closure and a reported compensation statement do not establish that every eligible consumer received adequate relief
events.source_and_uncertainty: Current CFPB ADSS payment-by-case page, retrieved 2026-09-18; reported compensation and route closure are not recipient-level outcomes

arrows.evidence: All three official pages identify a CFPB payment route and administrator or distribution status
arrows.counterexample: A formal route does not establish that the affected consumer used or received it
arrows.remaining_gap: Stable recipient linkage, issuance, delivery, amount, and failed-payment status

arrows.to: individual remedy receipt and account correction
arrows.evidence: BrightSpeed remains ongoing, Navient reports checks, and ADSS reports compensation and closure, but none publishes a recipient-level file
arrows.counterexample: Navient explicitly separates reported checks from reduction of the underlying student-loan obligation
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient receipt, amount, timing, returned payment, balance/credit correction, and remaining loss

arrows.to: restored financial security, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official pages contain no later recipient-level financial, behavioral, trust, or exit follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Payment can coexist with an unchanged obligation, residual loss, or no change in provider use
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-recipient follow-up on correction, residual burden, continued use, switching, trust, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes three official named CFPB redress routes at aggregate or administrator status. It does not claim individual receipt, adequate compensation, account correction, recovery, trust change, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact page-derived route fields, source URLs, and explicit uncertainty are retained; no administrator file, recipient-level data, or raw payment file is downloaded.
